scope: Primary methodological sources for coordination that preserves local perspectives, disagreement, common public facts, explicit local objectives, common information spaces, and inspectable joint action.
fixture_translation: The Gate12 fixture gives both local references the same public export-mode facts; their detail-versus-speed objective functions produce incompatible judgments. No hidden or asymmetric local source facts are being modeled.
execution_policy: Read-only primary-source review; no implementation, browser study, deployment, recruitment, external messages, or human-participant claims.

primary_sources.title: Institutional Ecology, 'Translations' and Boundary Objects: Amateurs and Professionals in Berkeley's Museum of Vertebrate Zoology, 1907-39
primary_sources.source_type: peer-reviewed research article; publisher DOI primary attribution and original-paper PDF copy
claims_used: Boundary objects can adapt to several local viewpoints while retaining a common identity across sites.
Standardization and translation are described as ways heterogeneous actors cooperate despite divergent viewpoints.
primary_sources.gate12_use: Treat the joint decision record as a stable shared object while retaining each local reference, judgment, provenance pointer, and unresolved incompatibility.
primary_sources.limits: A historical museum case and conceptual account; it does not establish shared human understanding or the instrument's coordination effects.

primary_sources.title: Taking CSCW Seriously: Supporting Articulation Work
primary_sources.source_type: journal article; publisher DOI primary attribution and author-uploaded full text
claims_used: Articulation work coordinates steps under local contingencies and incommensurate opinions.
A common database is not automatically a common information space; meaning is interpreted and negotiated locally and temporarily.
primary_sources.gate12_use: Record local references and judgments before the joint action; distinguish shared artifacts from shared meaning and preserve unresolved conflicts.
primary_sources.limits: Programmatic CSCW framework, not a controlled evaluation of this instrument or a measured human coordination benefit.

primary_sources.title: Coordination with Local Information
primary_sources.source_type: peer-reviewed formal research article; publisher DOI primary attribution and corrected institutional PDF
claims_used: In a finite-player global-games model, local signals observed by subsets of agents can produce multiple equilibria.
The pattern and reach of information sharing affect coordination determinacy.
primary_sources.gate12_use: Adjacent context only: keep the fixture's common public facts explicit, represent its distinct local objective functions explicitly, and reject any silent inference from a joint action to a single shared judgment.
primary_sources.limits: Formal strategic model with specific local-information and game assumptions; it is neither the implemented Gate12 model nor evidence for its objective-disagreement fixture or any human outcome.

derived_gate12_requirements.design: Freeze common public export facts, then at least two local reference functions/objectives and judgments; retain source, revision, function/objective, judgment, and incompatibility records before constructing the joint action.
derived_gate12_requirements.basis: Star and Griesemer (1989); Schmidt and Bannon (1992)

derived_gate12_requirements.design: The joint action lists participating judgments, decision scope, provenance, and unresolved disagreement; it may coordinate a next step without making local judgments identical.

Mark all source facts as common public inputs and local reference functions/objectives as distinct; declare every merge, omission, or tie-break rule in the finite menu and do not infer a shared judgment from action alone.
derived_gate12_requirements.basis: Dahleh et al. (2015/2016); Schmidt and Bannon (1992)

derived_gate12_requirements.design: Equivalent diagram and plain views must retain identical local references, disagreement records, joint-action fields, and provenance.
derived_gate12_requirements.basis: Source synthesis constrained to the frozen software instrument

limits: These sources motivate formal preservation and coordination checks; Dahleh et al. is adjacent local-information context, not the implemented objective-disagreement model or evidence for it.
The software fixture uses common public source facts with distinct local objectives; it does not implement private or asymmetric local source information.
Any human coordination claim requires actual participants, separate local judgments, and observed joint outcomes under a separately approved protocol.
Agreement is not the sole success criterion: preserved disagreement plus an inspectable bounded joint action is a distinct software outcome.
